recap:
Joe brings on Shane Smith, the legendary co-founder of VICE Media and seasoned journalist who built one of the most influential alternative media empires from nothing. This is a fascinating conversation about the evolution of media, what it takes to get real stories from dangerous places, and how journalism has fundamentally changed in the digital age.

Shane walks through his journey starting VICE as a scrappy magazine focused on youth culture and how it evolved into a full-scale media operation with global reach. He talks about the mentality needed to actually go places other journalists won't go, getting access to leaders and conflict zones that most media outlets can't touch. The guy basically built his reputation on being willing to show up places that were too risky or too politically charged for traditional outlets.

There's solid discussion around how media companies need to adapt or die, and how the old guard of journalism really struggled to understand what audiences actually wanted. Shane's perspective on building VICE as a vertical media company that could do everything from short-form clips to long-form documentaries was way ahead of its time. He talks about the business side of media too, not just the editorial side.

Toward the end they get into Shane's new podcast project 'Shane Smith Has Questions' which sounds like it'll be him doing what he does best: asking the hard questions to interesting people. Joe and Shane vibe on the future of independent media and how creators now have more power and reach than traditional gatekeepers ever did. It's the kind of conversation that shows why Shane became such a key figure in reshaping how news and content gets created and distributed.
